newsitem.title: UK: Uganda still working on Swiss bid for coffee unit.
newsitem.headline: Uganda still working on Swiss bid for coffee unit.

text.p: The Ugandan government has asked Swiss company Sucafina to extend the validity of its bid for a 51-percent stake in Uganda Coffee Marketing Board Limited (CMBL), contrary to earlier reports that it had rejected it.

In a letter received on Wednesday, William Okecho, coordinator of the privatisation of CMBL in Uganda, said the government needed 60 more days to analyse Sucafina's proposal. A final decision might not be due by December 26 which is when Sucafina's offer expires, it said.
Sources close to the company said the bid was still under consideration and had not been rejected as previously suggested.

On December 5, the minister of state responsible for privatisation, Matthew Rukikaire, had told Reuters Sucafina's bid of $3.3 million was turned down on grounds that it was too low when compared with assets of $36.7 million.
CMBL's principal asset is its central processing and storage unit in Bugoolobi. It has export processing capacity of four million 60-kg bags a year.
Rukikaire said a foreign buyer would have to offer at least two thirds of the $36.7 million, but that the government would favour local bidders instead.

Sucafina was the only bidder when the offer was closed on September 26. But Rukikaire said his privatisation unit was analysing proposals by a group of Ugandan investors interested in buying the shares.
It was not clear whether there were other formal bids in the pipeline.
